description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various models and configurations on a morphosyntactic probing task, with the y-axis representing accuracy on a scale from 70 to 95. The x-axis displays different model types and modifications, including "embedding," "1st layer," "random layers," "random layers +B2," "random layers +L2," "random layers +R2," "random layers +permute," "random," "random +B2," "random +L2," "random +R2," "random +permute," and "unperturbed." The chart shows that the "unperturbed" model achieves the highest accuracy, with a value of approximately 91.5. The "embedding" and "1st layer" models have similar accuracies, both around 83.5. The "random layers" models show a range of accuracies, with "random layers +B2" and "random layers +L2" having accuracies around 82.5, while "random layers +R2" and "random layers +permute" have accuracies around 81.5. The "random" models have lower accuracies, with "random" and "random +B2" having accuracies around 72.5, "random +L2" and "random +R2" having accuracies around 71.5, and "random +permute" having an accuracy around 72.5. The bars are color-coded, with the "unperturbed" model in orange, the "embedding" and "1st layer" models in blue, the "random layers" models in green, and the "random" models in red and pink. The chart is sorted in descending order of accuracy, with the highest accuracy at the far right.
